articles.title: Mavericks fans demand punishment for Aaron Nesmith after Pacers star sends Cooper Flagg to locker room
articles.summary: Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg had to sit out for the entire second half of the game as he suffered a shoulder injury due to Aaron Nesmith’s reckless fou...
articles.body:
Dallas Mavericks star Cooper Flagg had to sit out for the entire second half of the game as he suffered a shoulder injury due to Aaron Nesmith's reckless foul on him towards the end of the second quarter.

Flagg was leading a fast break and on his way to score an easy basket. Nesmith followed Flagg and tried to get the block but, in the process, the Mavs star awkwardly landed on the floor, which led to an injury.

A scuffle broke out as the Mavericks players were angered by what Nesmith had done on the play. The score was 73-40 with less than a minute to play in the second quarter. It seemed like the Pacers guard fouled in frustration as Flagg was dominating the game, scoring 14 points but also stuffing the stat sheet with 5 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 steals.

He had a team high +/- of 34, which indicated how effective Flagg was on the night, but after falling awkwardly, he was unable to return to the game.

Fans want harsh punishment for Aaron Nesmith

Nesmith was punished with a Flagrant 1 foul and also given a technical for indulging in a scuffle with the Mavericks players. Naji Marshall was also handed a technical as he came in heated, trying to retaliate against Nesmith. The two had to be separated, which further increased the intensity of the game.

After the first half, it was reported that Flagg had suffered an injury to his left shoulder.

Despite the injury to their star, the Mavs took home a 121-105 win in Tyrese Haliburton's return to Indiana.

While Mavericks fans were happy to grab their first win of the season, they wanted major repercussions for Nesmith as he caused the injury to Flagg.

"Nesmith needs a 25-game suspension after that b*******," said one fan. While another added: "This dude is way too wild I loved his game and knew he'd be a decent player but he's way too crazy."

Someone also wrote: "This is such a dangerous and dirty play."

Another fan opined: "This should mean multiple games of suspension for Nesmith. What a cowardly c***, could have really f***** Flagg up."

"There's absolutely no need to make that foul when you're down 30+," added an account user on X.

Nesmith will have to pay a small amount for the technical foul he was assessed, along with Marshall. However, the league has not confirmed whether he would be further suspended for the play or would be fined. If Nesmith was assessed a Flagrant 2, he would have to immediately leave the game, but even then he would not be suspended as per NBA's rules.

articles.title: ‘You fell off’ – Kobe Bryant’s ex-teammate destroys Linda Cohn’s attempted jab at LeBron James
articles.summary: Former ESPN expert Linda Cohn gets brutally called out for her take on LeBron James’ viral US National Anthem controversy. Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron Jam...
articles.body:
Former ESPN expert Linda Cohn gets brutally called out for her take on LeBron James' viral US National Anthem controversy.

Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James is facing massive backlash for allegedly practicing his golf swing during the US National Anthem ahead of the team's game against the Cleveland Cavaliers.

Despite Donald Trump calling out James' actions, the 41-year-old simply brushed it off. However, the media refuses to forgive James for disrespecting America.

Former ESPN analyst Linda Cohn became the latest name to take a jab at the King, but she was quickly called out by Kobe Bryant's former teammate Matt Barnes.

Matt Barnes snaps at Linda Cohn for ignoring Donald Trump to take a shot at LeBron James

During a recent episode of her podcast, Cohn called out James for acting like a 'three-year-old kid' who couldn't stand still during the US National Anthem.

While Cohn thought she did the right thing by calling out the 4x NBA champion, she was quickly given a reality check by several big names, including Barnes.

"You have more issue w Bron doing this than you do w Trump s_______ on the people of this country. D___ you fell off," Matt Barnes wrote on Instagram.

Barnes wasn't alone in calling out Cohn; even Hollywood star Jamie Foxx snapped at the former ESPN personality for trying to 'bash' LeBron while hoping to become relevant again.

It will be interesting to see how the 66-year-old will respond to being called irrelevant over her James comments. Will she back down and apologise? Only time will tell.

articles.title: Jemele Hill calls out James Dolan’s ‘utterly despicable’ behaviour with Knicks staff
articles.summary: The New York Knicks players received their championship rings earlier this week but a lot of staff at Madison Square Garden are not expected to be given one....
articles.body:
The New York Knicks players received their championship rings earlier this week but a lot of staff at Madison Square Garden are not expected to be given one.

After a 53-year wait, the Knicks won the NBA championship by beating the San Antonio Spurs in this year's Finals.

The roster was subsequently handed their rings ahead of the season-opener against the Philadelphia 76ers. But The Athletic have now reported that the Knicks' assistant coaches did not get rings this week, while many employees at Madison Square Garden will not receive rings at all.

They stated: "The Knicks' assistant coaches did not receive their championship rings during Tuesday's ceremony, despite being handed ring boxes, according to league sources. Many longtime employees at Madison Square Garden will not receive rings at all, per team sources. Those employees got their hopes up in late September, when they were sent a fake championship ring offer as part of a phishing test."

Jemele Hill has now responded to that tweet from The Athletic to hit out at James Dolan.

She wrote: "James Dolan is determined to kill every good vibe around this team, and bring every piece of bad karma their way.

"This is just utterly despicable. He makes it so hard to want good things for the Knicks because he has such a long history of treating people so poorly."

Fans have also called out Dolan about the phishing email previously mentioned by The Athletic.

In the meantime, the Knicks are still searching for their first win of the season after losing to the Boston Celtics on Friday.

Week 9 of the Central Texas high school football season saw one of the Austin area's four remaining undefeated teams suffer its first loss while Westlake registered a huge district rivalry win over Lake Travis.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs. Cleveland Browns: Week 7 staff picks and predictions
articles.summary: The Titans Wire staff offer their picks and predictions ahead of a Week 7 game between the Tennessee Titans and Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans (1-5) will take on the Cleveland Browns (4-2) this Sunday afternoon at Nissan Stadium in their seventh game of the 2026 regular season.

Opening the week, the Titans were listed as 2-point home underdogs , but that line has shifted slightly with Tennessee now at +2.5 as of this writing.

How does the Titans Wire staff see this Week 7 battle shaking out? Here's a look at our picks and score predictions.

In what promises to be a defensive battle, the upstart Browns come into Nashville poised to continue their hot streak, but they'll run into a Titans franchise high off their first win. The Titans' offensive line will give Cam Ward just enough protection to hit paydirt, and the Titans' defense will force Deshaun Watson into multiple turnovers that decide the game. Tennessee pulls out a close 17-13 win over the Browns.

The Titans have had a chaotic week. They got their first win of the season and barely got to enjoy it before the Jordan Elliott incident came to light. They've had a few days to get through that now, and if Robert Saleh is doing his job, the players aren't even thinking about that anymore. The Browns have surprised me this season; the way Todd Monken has them playing is impressive. Their defense is going to be a problem for the Titans' offense, and if the Titans don't get out in front early, the Browns' defense will shut them down. However, the Browns can't sleep on the Titans' defense either, which hasn't let any team score more than 26 points this season. It's going to be a defensive battle throughout the game, and whichever defense holds out the longest is the team that wins. Considering the Titans' inability to win back-to-back games, I'm giving the edge to the Browns.

The Titans have made me look like a fool two weeks running, so take any prediction I make with a grain of salt at this point. However, with the offense starting to groove a bit, I think they'll win their second consecutive game against a Browns team that struggles to score and consistently finds themselves in close games. The home field advantage will give Tennessee the edge.

Can the Titans make it two in a row? The Browns are playing pretty solid football. They have a good defense, which will make life tough for Cam Ward and the Titans. I expect a low-scoring affair with Cleveland winning.

Coming off a six-sack performance, the Titans defense faces a Browns offense that has allowed Deshaun Watson to be the most sacked QB in the NFL this season. With the Titans gaining momentum with 19 second-half points in Indianapolis, expect another complementary level from all three phases to pull off another upset.

The Cleveland Browns have a legitimate opportunity to take down the Tennessee Titans this week, and it starts with a defense that has consistently given opposing offenses problems. Cleveland is allowing just 20.3 points per game and has recorded 19 sacks through six games, giving the Browns a major advantage against a Titans offense that has struggled to find consistency. With Deshaun Watson leading the offense and Quinshon Judkins expected to be available, Cleveland has an opportunity to establish the run, control the clock, and keep Tennessee's defense on the field. Although the Titans are coming off an impressive comeback victory over Indianapolis, the Browns have proven they can win close games, and if their defensive front can pressure Cam Ward and force a few mistakes, Cleveland should have what it takes to leave Nashville with another victory.

Even with the Titans coming off their first win, their struggling offense is going to have trouble against the Browns' defense. The Browns might very well be the surprise of the league at 4-2 so far. The Browns have won four of their last five, and I expect that to continue against the Titans on Sunday.

articles.title: New British number one Boulter loses Japan semi-final
articles.summary: New British number one Katie Boulter loses 6-1 6-4 to Czech doubles specialist Katerina Siniakova in the Japan Open semi-finals.
articles.body:
Katie Boulter has lost in the Japan Open semi-finals, in her first match since reclaiming the British number one spot from Sonny Kartal.

Kartal moved above Boulter in the world rankings by reaching the final of last week's Wuhan Open.

But Boulter's run to the last four in Osaka, which included a victory over Antonia Ruzic in the quarter-finals, will be enough for her to go back above Kartal when the rankings are next updated.

However, the 30-year-old missed the chance to reach the final, and a shot at a fifth WTA singles title, losing 6-1 6-4 to doubles world number one Siniakova.

Eighth seed Boulter rallied after being swept aside in the opening set, going a break up at the start of the second.

But Siniakova, also 30, maintained her bid for a first singles title in four years by claiming two hard-fought breaks of her own to wrap up victory in 85 minutes.

She will now play 2023 champion Ashlyn Krueger in Sunday's final after the 22-year-old American beat compatriot and top seed Ann Li 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 6-3.

articles.title: After reflection, Giants' Cam Skattebo says recent fumbles a mental issue
articles.summary: New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo took a week to reflect on his recent fumbles and attributed them to a mental issue, not a technique issue.
articles.body:
New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he used the past week to step back and address the mental side of his recent ball-security issues rather than treating them as a technique problem.

"I think I got taught a lesson," Skattebo told reporters on Friday. "I don't know if that's from them or from myself, but I kind of had to step back and look at it and figure out why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, corrected those things, worked on them. Ready to go back out there and play ball."

He described getting ahead of himself in some games this season and losing sight of the primary task at that moment.

"There were a couple of mishaps that happened and I think it was the mental part," Skattebo said. "You see, in (the Washington) game, I got really excited, really happy. I think I got a little ahead of myself during the end of that game. I lost the main purpose of the game, and it was to take care of the ball at that moment. And I lost it. I think just understanding the situation and the circumstances I'm in, taking care of the ball and I'll be fine."

Skattebo made clear he is not positioning himself for a larger role based on this week's work. He said he has not yet done anything to earn more responsibility and will simply maximize whatever snaps come his way Sunday.

"I didn't do anything yet," Skattebo said. "I took care of the ball during practice and whatever my role is on Sunday is going to be my role and I'm going to give it everything I've got."

That approach fits with how the running back group has responded to John Harbaugh's open competition for the workhorse job. Skattebo said he, Devin Singletary, and Tyrone Tracy Jr. entered the week with a shared mindset and have stayed in regular communication about how each likes to hit holes so the next man is prepared when one comes off the field.

"Whoever is going to carry the ball knows that the other two guys got their back," Skattebo said. "When that guy comes off the field, the next guy in is going to perform. The vibes have been great. We've been talking. We've been staying on the same page."

The three backs have also coordinated with the offensive line so blocking schemes and preferred paths stay aligned. Skattebo said that communication has been consistent this week and the group is ready to carry it into the game.

articles.title: 4 NHL Trade Ideas for the Teams That Missed Out on Connor Hellebuyck
articles.summary: The Connor Hellebuyck saga is finally over with Friday's trade that sent him from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils.
articles.body:
The Connor Hellebuyck saga is finally over with Friday's trade that sent him from the Winnipeg Jets to the New Jersey Devils.

While it is a huge deal for the Devils and could open a new window for Stanley Cup contention for them, an almost equally intriguing story is what the teams that missed out on Hellebuyck might do for a goalie option.

So let's take a look at a few teams that could have been in the running for Hellebuyck and try to come up with some options to help them fill their potential goalie needs.

The idea: Trade for Montreal Canadiens goalie Sam Montembeault

Not that the Rangers were ever seriously in the market for Hellebuyck given his contract situation, but they could be interested in adding another goalie given the season-ending injury to starter Igor Shesterkin.

They have recently been linked to Utah's Karel Vejmelka and Buffalo's Ukka-Pekka Luukkonen, but a lot of that could have been dependent on one of those teams actually landing Hellebuyck and no longer needing either goalie.

Both goalies are signed long-term to contracts worth north of $4 million per season.

While those are not small numbers, they should be manageable for long-term backups as the salary cap continues to rise.

The question is whether or not the Rangers actually need that.

Shesterkin is obviously locked in as their starter when he returns next season, and rookie Dylan Garand is showing he has a chance to be a viable NHL goalie and extremely cheap backup. Why give up more significant assets and take up more salary cap space if you don't need to do it?

What might make more sense for the Rangers is simply finding a short-term, rental option for the rest of this season.

One name that could be available and make sense: Montreal's Sam Montembeault. The Canadiens have two young goalies that they really like in Jakub Dobes and Jacob Fowler that should be the future, while Montembeault is in the final year of his contract and likely the odd man out. He has had some really good seasons in the past, and could be a solid veteran to accompany Garand for the foreseeable future.

The value here shouldn't be anything more than a draft pick.

Let's say the Rangers send one of their four third-round picks over the next two years and a later pick to the Canadiens for Montembeault.

The trade idea: Alexander Nikishin to Minnesota for Filip Gustavsson

Even though the Hurricanes have won over the years without making major investments in the goalie position, they were still a potential player for Hellebuyck and would have been a fascinating landing spot. It would have given Hellebuyck one of the best defensive teams to play behind that he has ever had in the NHL, and would have almost certainly made them the favorites to win a second straight Stanley Cup.

But the Hurricanes were not willing to meet Winnipeg's asking price in terms of forwards, which currently leaves them with Pyotr Kochetkov and Brandon Bussi in their net.

While Bussi played well enough to help them win the Cup a year ago, there are still some legitimate questions as to whether or not he can do that over a full season. He is off to a slow start so far this season and is far from a sure-thing as a regular option.

A goalie upgrade could be in the cards here, even if it is not one that is as exciting or impactful as Hellebuyck.

The great thing for Carolina is its system is so structured, so well played, and so steady that it really doesn't need a goalie that has to steal a lot of games. It just requires a goalie that will not lose games. There are a couple of intriguing veteran trade options out there.

One of the most intriguing: Minnesota's Filip Gustavsson.

Jesper Wallstedt has become the No. 1 starter in Minnesota, and while the Wild might like the idea of keeping both Wallstedt and Gustavsson long-term, that's probably not viable financially given Gustavsson's $6.8 million cap hit over the next four-and-a-half seasons and whatever Wallstedt's next contract looks like (probably not cheap).

Carolina has a great trade chip in defenseman Alexander Nikishin, and Minnesota might be in the market for a longer-term, young defense option given the uncertainty around the future of Quinn Hughes. Not that Nikishin would be a suitable Hughes replacement, but he certainly still has some untapped potential that could be of interest to the Wild.

He remains unsigned in Carolina as a restricted free agent, and it only seems to be a matter of when and where he gets traded as opposed to if he gets traded. Why not use him as part of a trade to get a long-term goalie option? Gustavsson has had some big years during his career and could do well playing behind Carolina's defensive structure.

The trade idea: 3-team trade idea involving Stuart Skinner and Karel Vejmelka

Utah missed out on one Winnipeg goalie, but maybe it could get a different one?

And maybe it could use that as an opportunity to move Karel Vejmelka's contract to another team (the Los Angeles Kings) that also missed out on Hellebuyck this week.

Here's how it works: Los Angeles trades Alex Turcotte to Winnipeg for Stuart Skinner, and then turns around and trades Skinner to Utah for Vejmelka.

You can throw in some draft pick compensation from each team to sweeten the pot as needed, but this is the bones of it. It allows a couple of players that might need a change of scenery to get one, and Utah gets to try a different goalie that, while inconsistent, is capable of putting together decent stretches when used correctly.

Winnipeg currently has three goalies on its NHL roster after the Hellebuyck trade, with Nico Daws joining Skinner and Clay Stevenson. That is probably not going to work long-term, and something is going to have to give. Stevenson is a talented player that should get an extended look before they have to make a decision on him as an unrestricted free agent after the season, and this would open the door for him to do that. While Skinner has had a nice start to the season, that might actually make him the most tradable goalie of the three still on Winnipeg's roster. Especially if it falls out of playoff contention as the season goes on.

Turcotte has simply not panned out as hoped in Los Angeles and could use a fresh start somewhere else. Even after adding Dawson Mercer in the Hellebuyck trade, Winnipeg should still be in the market for more forward depth, and Turcotte could be a low-risk, high-reward gamble.

Utah obviously has a lot of belief in Sebastian Cossa after trading a first-round pick for him over the summer, while its organizational belief in Vejmelka might be starting to fade given his struggles and general inconsistency over the past couple of years. Skinner doesn't exactly solve the inconsistency concern, but he is a cheaper option, on a shorter contract, and could create some more long-term flexibility.

The Kings have two veteran goalies on their roster in Darcy Kuemper and Anton Forsberg, but neither player has been close to good enough this season and both players are unrestricted free agents after this season. For all of their flaws, the Kings generally defend well and could create a favorable situation for Vejmelka to get back on the right track. The Kings mostly need a goalie that isn't going to lose games for them. It is a low bar, and one that should not be difficult to reach.

The Sabres might end up regretting not doing more to get Hellebuyck.

After a quiet offseason that only saw them subtract talent from the roster instead of adding to it, the Sabres are off to a slow start and have more questions than answers in net. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen has not played well, and seems to be a complete wild-card every season when it comes to what his performance will look like.

Getting a player like Hellebuyck would have not only been a boost to the roster, it would have given the fan base a needed lift as well. These people watched 14 years of rancid hockey, got a taste of success during the 2025-26 season, and were rewarded by a shockingly quiet and disappointing offseason that did nothing to make the NHL team better in the short-term.

There are not many great long-term options on the trade market right now for goalies, so the Sabres might have to turn their attention to more short-term options.

There a handful of pending UFA's that could be on their radar, ranging from Detroit's John Gibson, to Seattle's Philipp Grubauer, to St. Louis' Jordan Binnington.

Binnington is the option they should avoid.

But Gibson and Grubauer have had some solid performances in recent years behind sub-par defensive teams, and could both be on the market if their teams slip out of playoff contention (as both very easily could do over the coming weeks and months).

In both cases we might be talking about draft pick capital going back the other way, and probably not significant draft pick capital. Maybe a second-round pick. At most. Maybe a third-round pick and a later pick, or lower-tier prospect. It would not be an overly exciting move, and certainly not as exciting as Hellebuyck would have been, but it could at least offer a little bit of stability to a position that might be lacking it. At least for the short-term.

articles.title: Booking Rey Mysterio's Best Opponents For Rumored WWE Retirement Tour
articles.summary: When thinking of possible upcoming WWE retirements, Rey Mysterio doesn't top the list.
articles.body:
When thinking of possible upcoming WWE retirements, Rey Mysterio doesn't top the list.

But Mysterio has always had a way of jumping over things and stealing shows in a way that landed him in the WWE Hall of Fame, among his many accolades.

From the sounds of it, Mysterio is the big name hanging up the boots in 2027.

According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Sean Rueter of Cageside Seats), there has already been some motion in WWE as to how the company would present Mysterio's retirement in the ring next year.

Booking Mysterio's goodbye isn't that difficult. But this is WWE. Neither was John Cena's and we all saw how that went. Everyone also sees how so-so the booking has been since for Gunther, the guy doing the retiring.

Mysteiro will turn 52 in December and he's been on record saying that his body's slowing down, bringing his in-ring career to a close. Luckily for him (and fans), his farewell tour won't demand major in-ring stress.

After all, Mysterio is currently an on-screen AAA general manager. Bringing that role back to weekly WWE programming on one of the three big shows makes a bunch of sense.

Family helps here. Mysterio's daughter, Aalyah, is training at the WWE Performance Center. Using Mysterio in an almost managerial or mentor role to help introduce her to crowds properly would be a shrewd way to go, even if it's just on NXT episodes.

Of course, onlookers want to know about the in-ring stuff more.

The conversation must start with Dominik Mysterio. They've had their brush-ups before, since his son really started going on the active roster back in 2020 (has it really been that long already?). Those two linking up again is a must.

A lot of Cena's farewell tour was rekindling old, classic feuds. Even if it's just backstage segments or in-ring promos with surprises like Batista, Kurt Angle and Undertaker, to name a very few, it would be a nice ode to his legendary career. Add Randy Orton's name to Dominik's when it comes to actual matches, of course.

The other element of Cena's goodbye tour was paying it forward, or the so-called passing the torch. That's where the in-ring stuff would really come from with Mysterio.

It's timely, too. Amid Penta's shocking rise to Money in the Bank briefcase winner, Wrestling Observer Radio's Dave Meltzer (h/t WrestleZone's Ojas Kulkarni ) suggested that WWE is changing its approach to the better for Mexican stars.

Meaning, names like Penta, Dragon Lee or even a revived Sin Cara character, to name a very few, never mind the AAA ties now, could be viable options for this sort of idea.

Granted, all of this assumes Mysterio goes on a "tour" at all. Cena was an anomaly on this front. Maybe it's a one-off match, which means it would go to Dominik.

A fun idea there might be a "mask" or even career match. Obvious result, but it's felt obvious for about six years now that Dominik would be the one to retire Mysterio.

If WWE wants to really WWW'ify it, though, they could have their cake and eat it too by involving Gunther. The career-killing Gunther trying to cut in line and brutalizing Mysterio before Dominik makes the save and gets his own feud could put everyone over.

Speaking of putting people over, all of Mysterio's last match would be about Dominik. It's no secret he's had a mid year or so on the main roster. Morphing back into a beloved babyface by saving his dad, or going super-heat heel by stealing the mask…it all just works. It's not hard to pull off either route and, frankly, everyone already knows the actual matches will be classics.

One could argue for Penta doing the retiring, but the man is already main eventing specials in Mexico against Roman Reigns and winning briefcases. For all we know, he's going to shock win a top title very soon. He doesn't need the help at this point.

Fittingly, Mysterio's value to cruiserweights and the art of lucha libre around the globe is unquestioned. It would only be right that he uses his official goodbye to jump start Dominik's rise to the main-event scene to carry on in his stead.
